status: Undergraduate teaching drafts for original review candidates; no activation
principle: Building use and architectural style are separate; no isolated building certifies a neighbourhood planning ideology.

cards.title: Bauhaus-inspired design workshop
cards.description: Bauhaus design connected art, craft and industrial production. This example uses clear volumes, steel-and-glass facades and spaces shaped around their different functions.
look_for: Visible structure and occupied working rooms
cards.main_idea: Bring design, making and modern construction together.
cards.source_design: Original generated teaching design; not a reconstruction of the Dessau building

cards.title: De Stijl artist studio
cards.description: De Stijl developed in the Netherlands. Its architecture explores horizontal and vertical lines, interlocking planes and primary colours alongside white, grey and black. This example uses those relationships to connect indoor working space with its surroundings.
look_for: Open corner glazing and clear spatial relationships
cards.main_idea: Explore space as a composition of planes, lines and colour.
cards.source_design: Original generated teaching design; not a reconstruction of the Rietveld Schröder House

cards.title: Mughal-inspired reading pavilion
cards.description: Mughal architecture developed in South Asia, combining Persian, Timurid and regional South Asian traditions. This original pavilion explores an ordered composition of shaded arcades and roof forms. It represents one historical design influence, not all South Asian or Islamic architecture.
look_for: A clear relationship between shaded shelter and garden space
cards.main_idea: Organize sheltered space through rhythm, shade and a legible composition.
cards.source_design: Original generated teaching design; not a reconstruction of a named historic monument
